title: Aim a spring-balanced desk lamp so its beam lands on a dot in an open notebook, the shade at least 30 cm up
instruction: Light the notebook for reading: aim the lamp at the red dot, with the shade at least 30 cm above the desk.
context: Pulling a desk lamp over a book and tilting its shade until the light falls where you are reading is something almost everyone has done at home, in a dorm or at an office desk. A spring-balanced arm lamp holds whatever pose it is left in, but its joints are coupled and each has its own stiffness: a push on the shade alone swings the arm about its elbow instead of tilting the shade, so people steady the arm with one hand while the other tilts the shade, then let go without knocking the light off the page. Here the light itself is scored: where the shade's axis meets the page, after both hands are away and the lamp has settled.
setup: Positions in cm from the arm bases' midpoint, x forward and y toward the left arm, on a bare wooden desk. Lamp: an Anglepoise Type 75 desk lamp (black; aluminium shade 14.5 cm across the mouth and 19 cm tall, aluminium arms of 30.1 cm and 30.4 cm between pivots, cast-iron base 19.5 cm across; 3.1 kg; 6.5 W LED bulb), standing free with its base's centre at (58, -25). Its start pose: arm swung toward the robot's right, lower arm upright and upper arm sloping down, shade's mouth centre 16 cm above the desk at about (36, -16), tilted so the shade's axis meets the desk 13 cm from the dot. Notebook: a Moleskine Classic Notebook, Large, hard cover (13 x 21 cm, 240 pages, 0.33 kg), opened flat at its middle (26 x 21 cm, spine along x), centre at (30, 2), loose. Dot: a red 19 mm round paper sticker in the middle of the right-hand page, at (30, -4.5). Both grippers start open at the ready pose. The screenshot shows the start.
scoring: The beam's centre is where the shade's axis (the line through the middle of its mouth, square to the mouth) meets the page. Readings count once both hands have been clear of the lamp (each fingertip midpoint 5 cm or more from both arms and 11 cm or more from the shade's axis) and the lamp has not moved (no joint more than 0.3 degrees) for 3 s; a hand coming back, or the lamp moving, restarts the 3 s. Then: 1.0 if the beam's centre is within 30 mm of the dot's centre and the shade's mouth centre is at least 30 cm above the desk; 0.5 within 60 mm with the mouth at least 30 cm up; 0.25 within 100 mm, or within 60 mm with the mouth lower than 30 cm; otherwise 0, including a shade facing level or up. The trial scores 0 if the notebook or the lamp's base ends up moved more than 20 mm from its start, or either is tipped more than 3 degrees, or no 3 s clear and still period was reached. Doing nothing scores 0: the beam starts 13 cm from the dot. Real trial: with the robot stopped and its hands away for 3 s, the supervisor switches on a small dot laser fixed on the bulb's tip along the shade's axis (its battery box on the desk), measures from the red laser spot to the dot's centre with a steel ruler and photographs it from above; a tape measure from the desk to the middle of the shade's mouth gives the height; masking-tape outlines round the base and the notebook show whether either moved.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Set the lamp's base and the notebook back in their masking-tape outlines, and the lamp back to its start pose by a printed side-view template (the shade's mouth 16 cm up over a tape cross on the desk). Spring-scale test before a session, lamp in the goal pose: with the upper arm held, a level pull toward the base on the bottom of the shade's near rim tilts the shade at about 2.1 N; with the arm free the same pull swings the arm first, at about 1.8 N.
fidelity: True size from Anglepoise's dimensioned drawing and published reach. The springs are modelled as an ideal balance: arm and shade keep their mass but carry no weight, and joint friction holds any pose, as the real lamp does; spring rates are not published and the joint friction values are estimates. The lower arm's parallel rods are one rigid link. Light is not rendered: the beam is the shade's axis. The notebook is one rigid block.
scores: Scripted open-loop demo: 1.0 in five simulator runs (three cloud, two local, the latest on this revision's scorer). Dream-1 run: 0.0 (rerun on this revision).
